_meta.description: Normalized Cloudflare developer-platform pricing, harvested from the public docs. Each product's /pricing/ page was read as raw markdown (<page-url>index.md), extracted, and adversarially re-verified number-by-number. Intended as a base for cost / pricing models — not a billing oracle.
_meta.disclaimer: Prices change and regional/enterprise terms vary. Always reconcile against each product's pricing_url before billing. Figures were transcribed verbatim from the pricing tables; where included allotments and overage are quoted in different unit bases (e.g. GiB-hours included vs per-GiB-second overage on Containers), the per-meter `unit` records the overage unit and `notes` flag the mismatch — convert before doing math.

schema.product: id, name, category, doc_url, pricing_url, limits_url, source_confidence, plans[], meters[], catalog[]?, notes[]
schema.plan: key (free|paid|standard|enterprise|...), base_usd_month (fixed monthly platform fee; 0=free, null=N/A or contract), description
schema.meter: key, label, unit (billed unit, verbatim), free_included/free_period, paid_included/paid_period, overage_usd (USD per `overage_per` units beyond included), overage_per, notes
schema.catalog_item: item, unit, price_usd, per, notes — per-model/variant rate table (used by Workers AI, Images, Stream)

_meta.cost_model_hint: monthly_cost(product) ≈ plan.base_usd_month + Σ meters max(0, usage − paid_included) / overage_per × overage_usd. Free plan uses free_included/free_period instead. base_usd_month is charged once per account, not per product — most storage/AI products inherit the single $5 Workers Paid platform fee.

products.name: Workers

plans.description: Workers Free plan (default). Includes limited usage of Workers, Pages Functions, Workers KV and Hyperdrive. Requests limited to 100,000/day (resets at 00:00 UTC, Error 1027 when exceeded); 10 ms CPU time per invocation.

Workers Paid plan (Standard usage model). Minimum charge of $5 USD per month per account. Includes Workers, Pages Functions, Workers KV, Hyperdrive, and Durable Objects usage with increased initial allotments and clear per-unit overage. No additional charges for data transfer (egress) or throughput (bandwidth).
Workers Enterprise accounts are billed based on the usage model specified in their contract; no public price. Contact your Account Manager/account team.

meters.label: Requests
meters.notes: Standard usage model. Inbound requests to your Worker; Cloudflare does not bill for subrequests. A WebSocket connection is charged as one request (the initial Upgrade); WebSocket messages routed through a Worker do not count as requests. Requests to static assets are free and unlimited. Standard: 10 million included/month, +$0.30 per additional million. Confirmed verbatim in pricing table.

meters.label: CPU time
meters.notes: Standard usage model. Free plan: no monthly CPU-ms allotment, capped at 10 ms CPU time per invocation. Standard/Paid: 30 million CPU milliseconds included per month, +$0.02 per additional million CPU milliseconds. No charge or limit for duration (wall-clock time). Max 5 min CPU time per invocation (default 30 s); 15 min per Cron Trigger or Queue Consumer invocation. paid_included is in CPU milliseconds (30,000,000 = 30M CPU ms); overage_per is 1,000,000 CPU ms. Confirmed verbatim.

meters.label: Workers Logs — Log Events Written
meters.notes: Workers Logs is included in both Free and Paid plans. Free: 200,000 log events/day, 3-day retention. Paid: 20 million included/month, +$0.60 per additional million, 7-day retention. free_included is per day; paid_included and overage_per are event counts. Confirmed verbatim in Workers Logs table.

meters.label: Workers Trace Events Logpush — Requests
meters.notes: Workers Trace Events Logpush is only available on the Workers Paid plan. 10 million requests/month included, +$0.05 per additional million. Charges apply to request logs that reach the end destination after applying filtering or sampling. Confirmed verbatim in Workers Trace Events Logpush table.

notes: All fields independently re-derived and confirmed verbatim against https://developers.cloudflare.com/workers/platform/pricing/index.md (page dateModified 2026-04-23 per embedded schema.org metadata). No numbers were changed; the draft was accurate.

Core Workers compute is billed under the Standard usage model on two metrics: Requests and CPU time. Legacy usage models (Workers Bundled, Workers Unbound) are deprecated; users are advised to move to Standard. Changing usage model only affects billable usage, no technical implications. Standard pricing migration occurred March 1, 2024.
No additional charges for data transfer (egress) or throughput (bandwidth) on Workers. All included usage is monthly (except Free daily limits, which reset at 00:00 UTC).

Requests to static assets are free and unlimited (confirmed by Example 2: a project with 12M static-asset requests + 3M dynamic Worker requests using 7 ms CPU each stays at the $5.00 base subscription).

Requests made from one Worker to another via a Service Binding do not incur additional request fees — billed as one request (initial invocation) plus combined CPU time across both Workers. Only on Standard pricing; on deprecated Bundled/Unbound, Service-Binding requests are charged as separate requests.
All Pages Functions are billed as Workers; the same pricing and inclusions apply. See https://developers.cloudflare.com/pages/functions/pricing/ .

The Workers pricing page also documents adjacent products billed under the Workers Paid plan but priced separately, each with its own dedicated pricing page: Workers KV, Hyperdrive, Queues, D1, Durable Objects, Vectorize, R2, and Containers. These are captured as their own product entries and are intentionally NOT duplicated in these Workers meters (which cover core Workers compute + Workers-native observability: Workers Logs and Workers Trace Events Logpush).

Example pricing (from docs, confirmed): 15M requests/month at 7 ms CPU each on Paid = $5.00 subscription + $1.50 requests ((15M-10M)/1M*$0.30) + $1.50 CPU (((7ms*15M)-30M)/1M*$0.02) = $8.00 total. 100M requests/month at 7 ms = $5.00 + $27.00 + $13.40 = $45.40 total. A Cron Worker at 720 req/month with 3 min (180,000 ms) CPU each = $5.00 + $0.00 requests + $1.99 CPU = $6.99.

Custom CPU-time limits can be set per Worker (Wrangler `limits` config or dashboard Settings > CPU Limits) to prevent runaway bills / denial-of-wallet attacks. Workers migrated from the legacy Bundled model before the March 1, 2024 Standard migration got an automatic 50 ms CPU limit.

Limits page (https://developers.cloudflare.com/workers/platform/limits/) confirms: Free 100,000 requests/day vs Paid no limit; CPU time 10 ms (Free) vs 5 min max (Paid, default 30 s); average Worker uses ~2.2 ms CPU/request.

products.name: Durable Objects

plans.description: Workers Free plan. Only SQLite-backed Durable Objects are available (key-value backend is Paid-only). Daily free-tier limits reset at 00:00 UTC; exceeding any one free limit fails further operations of that type.

Workers Paid plan. SQLite or key-value storage backend available. All pricing examples add a 'minimum $5/mo usage' Workers Paid base fee. Overage rates for compute and storage apply beyond the included allotments. base_usd_month=5 reflects that minimum monthly usage floor.

meters.label: Requests
meters.notes: Confirmed in compute-billing table: Free 100,000/day; Paid 1 million/month + $0.15/million. Includes HTTP requests, RPC sessions, WebSocket messages, and alarm invocations. Each RPC session is billed as one request (subsequent calls on a returned stub are part of the same session, not billed separately). A request is needed to create a WebSocket connection; no charge for outgoing WebSocket messages or incoming protocol pings. For compute-billing only, incoming WebSocket messages use a 20:1 ratio (100 incoming messages billed as 5 requests); the 20:1 ratio does not affect metrics/analytics.

meters.label: Duration
meters.notes: CORRECTED: unit is GB-s (draft said 'million GB-s' but the included values 13,000 and 400,000 are raw GB-s, not millions). Confirmed in compute-billing table: Free 13,000 GB-s/day; Paid 400,000 GB-s/month + $12.50 per MILLION GB-s (hence overage_per=1,000,000). Wall-clock compute duration while the Object is active or idle-but-not-hibernatable. Duration billing charges for the 128 MB memory allocated regardless of actual usage. Objects idle and eligible for hibernation are not billed for duration.

meters.label: Rows read (SQLite storage backend)
meters.notes: Confirmed in SQLite-backend table: Free 5 million/day; Paid first 25 billion/month included + $0.001 per million rows. SQLite storage billing enabled January 2026 (target Jan 7, 2026); only usage on/after the target date incurs charges. Rates match D1 pricing. Key-value methods (get/put/delete/list) query a hidden SQLite table and are billed as rows read/written.

meters.label: Rows written (SQLite storage backend)
meters.notes: Confirmed in SQLite-backend table: Free 100,000/day; Paid first 50 million/month included + $1.00 per million rows. Each setAlarm() is billed as a single row written; deletes are counted as rows written. Rates match D1 pricing. Billing enabled Jan 2026 (target Jan 7, 2026).

meters.label: SQL Stored data (SQLite storage backend)
meters.notes: Confirmed in SQLite-backend table: Free 5 GB (total); Paid 5 GB-month included + $0.20 per GB-month. Storage billing enabled January 2026 (target Jan 7, 2026). Empty SQLite database ~12 KB; metadata in internal tables counts toward billable storage until deleteAll(). Note free_period is labeled 'total' on Free plan rather than a recurring month; kept as 'month' per schema, but the 5 GB is a total cap capped further by the 5 GB Free account limit.

meters.label: Read request units (key-value storage backend)
meters.notes: Confirmed in key-value-backend table (Workers Paid plan only; not available on Free): 1 million included + $0.20 per million. A request unit is 4 KB of data read; reads >4 KB consume multiple units. List operations billed by read request units based on data examined (e.g., 80 KB returned = 20 read request units; an empty list = 1 read request unit).

meters.label: Write request units (key-value storage backend)
meters.notes: Confirmed in key-value-backend table (Workers Paid plan only): 1 million included + $1.00 per million. A request unit is 4 KB written; writes >4 KB consume multiple units (a 9 KB write = 3 write request units). Each setAlarm is billed as a single write request unit.

meters.label: Delete requests (key-value storage backend)
meters.notes: Confirmed in key-value-backend table (Workers Paid plan only): 1 million included + $1.00 per million. Delete requests are unmetered by size (deleting a 100 KB value is charged one delete request).

meters.label: Stored data (key-value storage backend)
meters.notes: Confirmed in key-value-backend table (Workers Paid plan only): 1 GB included + $0.20 per GB-month. Billed until data is removed.

notes: Durable Objects incur two billing types: compute (requests + duration) and storage. Storage pricing depends on backend: SQLite-backed (recommended; available on Free and Paid) or key-value-backed (Workers Paid only).
All pricing examples add a 'minimum $5/mo usage' Workers Paid base fee; base_usd_month=5 on the paid plan reflects this usage floor.
Workers Free plan supports only SQLite-backed Durable Objects. To downgrade from Paid to Free, all key-value-backed namespaces must be deleted first.

CORRECTION vs draft: the Duration meter unit is GB-s, not 'million GB-s'. The table's included values are 13,000 GB-s/day (Free) and 400,000 GB-s/month (Paid); the $12.50 overage is per MILLION GB-s (overage_per=1,000,000).

Duration is billed for the 128 MB memory allocated per Object regardless of actual usage; hibernation-eligible idle Objects are not billed for duration. An active outbound connection keeps a DO in memory and incurs duration for up to 15 minutes per connection.
SQLite rows-read/rows-written included limits and rates match D1 pricing. Key-value methods (get/put/delete/list) hit a hidden SQLite table and bill as rows read/written on SQLite-backed DOs.
SQLite storage billing (rows read, rows written, SQL stored data) will be enabled January 2026 with a target date of Jan 7, 2026 (no earlier); only usage on/after the target date incurs charges.

Account limits (limits page): Max Durable Object classes per account = 500 (Workers Paid) / 100 (Free). SQLite storage per account = Unlimited (Paid) / 5 GB (Free). Storage per Durable Object = 10 GB (SQLite table, flat — NOT differentiated by plan; the draft's claim of '1 GB on Free per DO' is unconfirmed, Free is bounded by the 5 GB account cap instead). Key-value backend: storage per account 50 GB (raisable). CPU per request 30s default, configurable to 5 min active CPU. Durable Objects are Workers and inherit Workers per-invocation limits.
Free-tier daily limits reset at 00:00 UTC; exceeding any single free limit fails further operations of that type.

notes: VERIFIED against https://developers.cloudflare.com/containers/pricing/index.md — every meter number, unit, overage rate, and inclusion confirmed verbatim in the pricing tables (no draft corrections needed).
Containers require the Workers Paid plan ($5 USD/month); the Free plan lists Memory and CPU as N/A and leaves Disk blank.

Containers are billed for every 10ms that they are actively running. Charges start when a request is sent to the container or when it is manually started, and stop after the container instance goes to sleep (scale-to-zero after a timeout).
Memory and disk usage are based on the provisioned resources of the selected instance type; CPU usage is based on active usage only.

IMPORTANT unit-basis note: included allotments in the docs are stated in GiB-hours (memory), vCPU-minutes (CPU), and GB-hours (disk), while overage prices are per GiB-second, vCPU-second, and GB-second respectively. Each meter's `unit` records the per-second overage unit verbatim; `paid_included` (25/375/200) retains the docs' hour/minute basis noted per-meter.

Predefined instance types (vCPU / Memory / Disk): lite = 1/16 vCPU / 256 MiB / 2 GB; basic = 1/4 vCPU / 1 GiB / 4 GB; standard-1 = 1/2 vCPU / 4 GiB / 8 GB; standard-2 = 1 vCPU / 6 GiB / 12 GB; standard-3 = 2 vCPU / 8 GiB / 16 GB; standard-4 = 4 vCPU / 12 GiB / 20 GB. Custom instance types also supported (min 1 / max 4 vCPU, max 12 GiB memory, max 20 GB disk; min 3 GiB memory per vCPU; max 2 GB disk per 1 GiB memory). Note: `dev` and `standard` are backward-compat aliases for `lite` and `standard-1`.

Additional billing beyond Containers' own rates: incoming requests are handled by your Worker (Workers pricing) and each container has its own Durable Object (Durable Objects pricing) — both billed separately. Container logs are billed at the Workers Logs rate.

Account-level limits (from limits page, dateModified 2026-06-08): Concurrent memory 6 TiB, Concurrent vCPU 1,500, Concurrent disk 30 TB, Total image storage per account 50 GB, Image size same as instance disk space.
Pricing page dateModified: 2026-04-21; limits page dateModified: 2026-06-08.

products.name: Workflows

plans.description: Workers Free plan — Workflows included; shares Workers daily request/CPU limits

Workers Paid plan — Workflows included; billed identically to Workers Standard on requests, CPU time, and storage. NOTE: the Workflows pricing page does not state a base fee verbatim; the $5/mo is the Workers Paid platform fee inherited via the page's explicit statement that 'Workflows pricing is identical to Workers Standard pricing.'

meters.label: Requests (millions)
meters.notes: Confirmed verbatim in pricing table. Requests = Workflow invocations (triggering a new instance). Steps within a Workflow are not invocations, and subrequests made from a Workflow do not incur additional request costs. Free tier's '100,000 per day' is shared with Workers requests. Paid: '10 million included per month + $0.30 per additional million'.

meters.label: CPU time (ms)
meters.notes: Confirmed verbatim. Free plan: '10 milliseconds of CPU time per invocation' — a per-invocation cap, NOT a monthly pool (hence free_period=null; free_included=10 is a per-invocation ms limit). Paid: '30 million CPU milliseconds included per month + $0.02 per additional million CPU milliseconds' — paid_included and overage_per are in raw CPU milliseconds; overage_usd is $0.02 per 1,000,000 CPU ms. CPU time is active compute only — idle/sleeping/waiting instances do not incur CPU time.

meters.label: Storage (GB-mo)
meters.notes: Confirmed verbatim. Free plan: '1GB' (a hard cap, not a metered monthly pool). Paid plan: '1GB included per month + $0.20/ GB-month'. GB-month = average of peak storage per day over a 30-day billing period. Storage counts across all instances (running, errored, sleeping, completed). Billed identically to Durable Objects SQL storage backend. Storage billing went live September 15th, 2025. On the Free plan, attempting to store state past the limit throws an error.

notes: Verified against https://developers.cloudflare.com/workflows/reference/pricing/index.md (dateModified 2026-05-04) and .../limits/index.md (dateModified 2026-06-15). All three meter rows confirmed verbatim from the 'Workflows Pricing' table.

Workflows pricing is identical to Workers Standard pricing and billed on three dimensions: CPU time, Requests (invocations), and Storage. Per the page's FAQ 'How do Workflows show up on my bill?': Workflows are billed AS Workers and share the same CPU time and request SKUs — they show up on the bill as Workers, not as a separate line item.
FAQ 'Are there additional costs for Workflows?': No. Priced on the same compute (CPU time) and requests (invocations) as Workers, plus storage (state from a Workflow).
A Workflow that is waiting on an API response, paused via step.sleep, or otherwise idle does NOT incur CPU time.
Subrequests made from within a Workflow do not incur additional request costs.
CPU limit per Workflow invocation defaults to 30 seconds on Paid and is configurable up to 5 minutes via the limits.cpu_ms Wrangler property; Free plan is capped at 10 ms of CPU time per invocation.
Instance state retention: 3 days on Free, 30 days on Paid (configurable to a shorter period per instance via the retention option in WorkflowInstanceCreateOptions).

Free plan limits (from limits page): 100,000 Workflow executions per day (shared with Workers daily limit), 100 concurrent instances per account, 100MB max state per instance. Paid plan: unlimited executions, 50,000 concurrent instances per account, 1GB max state per instance.

Note on the $5 paid base fee: it is NOT stated on the Workflows pricing page itself — it is inherited from Workers Standard/Paid via the page's assertion that Workflows pricing is identical to Workers Standard pricing. Treat with medium confidence relative to the metered rates (which are high-confidence verbatim).
Pricing page dateModified: 2026-05-04; Limits page dateModified: 2026-06-15.

Sending to verified destination addresses in your account is free on ALL plans (including when only Email Routing is configured) and does not count toward the 3,000 monthly included quota or the daily sending limits.
Inbound emails (Email Routing) are Unlimited on both Workers Free and Workers Paid.

Email Routing Workers (Workers that handle incoming emails) are billed according to Workers pricing (https://developers.cloudflare.com/workers/platform/pricing/), not by Email Service directly. On the Workers Free plan, complex email handlers may hit the EXCEEDED_CPU limit.

The Workers Paid base platform fee (commonly $5/month per Workers pricing) is referenced via a link but NOT stated verbatim on the Email Service pricing page, so paid base_usd_month is left null here rather than asserting an unconfirmed number.

New accounts start with a conservative daily sending quota that scales up automatically based on sending behavior, deliverability rates, and account standing (Limits page). Higher limits can be requested via the Limit Increase Request Form (https://forms.gle/eX6pXvit1wBv77Yw5).

Email content limits (Limits page): 50 recipients per email (to+cc+bcc combined), 998-char subject (RFC 5322), 5 MiB total message size including attachments (25 MiB for verified destination addresses only), 16 KB combined custom-header size.

Zone/routing limits (Limits page): 30 domains per zone (Email Routing + Email Sending combined, including apex); 200 routing rules per domain; 200 destination addresses per account (shared across all domains); 25 MiB inbound message size; 100 Reply References entries (message.reply() throws above this).

products.name: Logs (Logpush)

plans.description: Logpush is available only on the Enterprise plan (Availability table on the Logpush overview: Free=No, Pro=No, Business=No, Enterprise=Yes). No public standalone dollar price is published in the Logs docs; pricing is bundled into the Enterprise plan. The Logs index links out to general Cloudflare pages for pricing (Plans -> https://www.cloudflare.com/products/cloudflare-logs/, Pricing -> https://www.cloudflare.com/plans/#overview). Documented exception: Workers Trace Events Logpush is available to non-Enterprise customers on the Workers Paid plan.

meters.label: Max Logpush jobs per zone
meters.notes: Verbatim from the Logpush overview (## Limits): 'There is currently a max limit of 4 Logpush jobs per zone. Trying to create a job once the limit has been reached will result in an error message: creating a new job is not allowed: exceeded max jobs allowed.' This is a hard cap on the Enterprise plan, NOT a billable/overage meter. Logpush itself has NO published per-unit (per-GB / per-log / per-request) usage price anywhere in the Cloudflare Logs docs.

notes: Cloudflare Logs / Logpush has NO dedicated usage-based pricing page in the Logs documentation. Confirmed against https://developers.cloudflare.com/logs/llms.txt (fetched 2026-07-02): no /pricing/ or /limits/ page path exists in the entire Logs docs tree. Logpush is billed as an Enterprise plan feature, not as a separately metered per-unit product.
Verbatim Availability table (Logpush overview, https://developers.cloudflare.com/logs/logpush/): Availability -> Free=No, Pro=No, Business=No, Enterprise=Yes.

Documented exception to Enterprise-only availability (verbatim note on the Logpush overview): 'Users without an Enterprise plan can still access Workers Trace Events Logpush by subscribing to the Workers Paid plan.' So a narrow non-Enterprise path exists, but no free tier for general Logpush.

General FAQ (https://developers.cloudflare.com/logs/faq/general-faq/) confirms: 'Are logs available for customers who are not on an Enterprise plan? Not yet, but we are planning to make them available to other customer plans in the future.' No pricing figures in the FAQ.

The Logs index page (https://developers.cloudflare.com/logs/) 'More resources' section links out for pricing: Plans -> https://www.cloudflare.com/products/cloudflare-logs/ and Pricing -> https://www.cloudflare.com/plans/#overview. No per-unit rate card is published in the developer docs.
Only concrete numeric limit found in docs (verbatim): 'There is currently a max limit of 4 Logpush jobs per zone.'

When Logpush delivers to Cloudflare R2 (destination docs: https://developers.cloudflare.com/logs/logpush/logpush-job/enable-destinations/r2/), any storage/egress costs are billed under R2's own pricing, not under a Logpush meter. No Logpush-specific charge is stated.
Logs Engine (R2 Log Retrieval, https://developers.cloudflare.com/logs/r2-log-retrieval/) is being superseded by Log Explorer; its docs contain no pricing figures.
No Enterprise dollar figure is published in the docs, so plans[].base_usd_month is null (HARD RULE: never write a number not read verbatim).
